content.text: Carmen confronts financier J. Wilton Ames, rejecting his money, power, and marriage proposal. She rescues his addicted son Sidney through Christian Science, then investigates poverty and exploitation at Ames’s Avon mills and Washington politics. Her reports expose corruption, prompting strikes, violence, massacre, and Carmen’s arrest. At the Ketchim trial, a locket reveals Carmen is Ames’s daughter and Spanish royalty; Ames collapses. Carmen stays beside him in his mansion’s sickroom, helping transform him into a remorseful reformer. Meanwhile, Hitt travels to Cartagena, where he and Don Jorge rescue imprisoned priest Jose de Rincon from San Fernando. Carmen reunites with Jose and his child. Later, Ames supports restitution, reforms Avon, revives the Express, and joins the group’s spiritual mission centered on love, Christian healing, and overcoming materialism.
